summary: Risk-off (confidence 0.45) held up on day one of the 5-session window. SPY's benchmark value fell from 560.38 to 539.98 (-3.64%), which puts SPY near 690, about 5.5% under its 200-day (730.19 in the morning packet). The cross-asset pieces held too. TLT, bought today, rose 1.23% while stocks fell, so duration hedged again. WMT (+1.69%) and KR (+0.74%) rose, consistent with the Staples tilt, while IDXX (-2.17%), MSCI (-2.22%) and INCY (-1.69%) fell. The open-print exits of VOO (656.09) and VTI (351.29) sat only about 0.3% under the 11-19 closes, so most of the day's drop happened after the book left. This is one session and is not graded. To end the window wrong, SPY needs to close above about 708.7 (within 1% of 715.87) at session 5, a rebound of roughly 2.7% from here.
broken_theses: Partly: the Staples tilt was not uniform. SAM fell 5.00% on the day (the founder-CEO handover 8-K 5.02 is the likely single-name cause, but I can't verify that from my inputs), so 'favor Staples' held for WMT and KR, not for every name in the bucket.

Not tested: my main counter-argument (credit had not cracked, HYG 5d -0.58%, so a sharp bounce was possible) is the reason confidence was 0.45. close.json carries no HYG, LQD, RSP or VIXY figures, so I can't say whether credit cracked today. The next packet has to settle it.
update: Keep risk-off going into the next run unless the 11-20 packet shows HYG holding flat while VIXY's 5-day gain fades and SPY recovers more than half of today's loss. A 3.6% one-day fall with no credit stress is the setup in which my 11-06 risk-off call graded wrong (+2.59% bounce). Raise confidence only if HYG's 5d is worse than about -1.5% or RSP closes below its 200-day (it was 1.70% above). On defensives, today supports 'Treasuries are hedging' (TLT +1.23% vs SPY -3.64%), but that is a second week of evidence, not a trend. If TLT and IEF fall with stocks on any run, I'll move the defensive preference to SHY/cash, which is the TLT thesis's own clause. Keep gold and crypto as 'not hedges' until GLD's 5-day return turns up against a falling SPY. On the scorecard, my 0.556 hit rate beats the 0.444 always-risk-off baseline by only two calls, so the next stance has to rest on the new packet and not on today's move continuing. No Reviewer lesson names the Market Analyst, so none shaped this review.
